g.title: Status_Epilepticus_QSP_Model
g.text: Status epilepticus is not a long seizure. It is a
: the drug target is leaving the synapse while the clinician decides what to give.
ONE clock drives TWO receptor movements in OPPOSITE directions (synaptic γ2-GABA-A out, synaptic NMDA in), so benzodiazepine efficacy DECAYS and ketamine efficacy GROWS along the same time axis.
A third pool — extrasynaptic δ-GABA-A — is not internalised at all, which is why the drugs that survive benzodiazepine failure are the ones that never depended on the pool that was lost.
Everything downstream (the ESETT three-way tie, RAMPART's IM-beats-IV result, the subtle-SE response collapse, the negative allopregnanolone trial) is arithmetic on those three pools plus one delay.

g.title: cluster_etio
g.text: 🧨 1. Aetiology — sets DRIVE (the term drugs must out-suppress). Refractoriness = DRIVE > maximal achievable SUPPRESSION, not 'wrong drug chosen'

g.title: cluster_net
g.text: 🕸️ 2. Cortico-hippocampal network — self-sustainment is a BISTABLE switch. Once E-feedback gain > 1, removing the trigger no longer stops the seizure

g.title: cluster_gabatraf
g.text: ⏱️ 3. THE CLOCK, arm 1 — SYNAPTIC γ2-GABA-A RECEPTORS ARE INTERNALISED. This is the whole benzodiazepine story: the target itself is a decaying resource

g.title: cluster_delta
g.text: 🛡️ 4. THE POOL THAT STAYS — extrasynaptic α4/α6βδ GABA-A is NOT internalised (some evidence it INCREASES). Every drug that still works late acts here or downstream of the receptor

g.title: cluster_nmda
g.text: ⏱️ 5. THE CLOCK, arm 2 — NMDA RECEPTORS MOVE INTO THE SYNAPSE. Same clock, opposite sign: this is why ketamine is the only drug that gets BETTER with delay

g.title: cluster_cl
g.text: 🧂 6. Chloride homeostasis — KCC2 down-regulation makes GABA-A opening DEPOLARISING. A fourth failure mode that no GABAergic drug can fix

g.title: cluster_endog
g.text: ⚖️ 7. Endogenous neuropeptide balance — the brain's own OFF switch is consumed while its ON switch is up-regulated (a second, slower clock)

g.title: cluster_infl
g.text: 🔥 8. Neuroinflammation + BBB opening — a slow loop that both sustains the seizure and writes the chronic epilepsy that follows

g.title: cluster_injury
g.text: 💀 9. Excitotoxic neuronal injury — a SEPARATE integrator. 'Seizure stopped' and 'brain undamaged' are two different endpoints with two different clocks

g.title: cluster_sys1
g.text: 🫀 10. Systemic PHASE I — COMPENSATED (≈ 0-30 min). Massive sympathetic surge keeps cerebral supply ahead of demand

g.title: cluster_sys2
g.text: 🩸 11. Systemic PHASE II — DECOMPENSATED (> ~30 min). Supply now falls while demand stays maximal: the systemic switch that mirrors the receptor switch

g.title: cluster_bzd
g.text: 💉 12. First line — BENZODIAZEPINES. Their PK differences are real but small; the variable that dominates outcome is the DELAY before the first adequate dose

g.title: cluster_second
g.text: ⚖️ 13. Second line — ESETT's three-way tie is a STRUCTURAL PREDICTION: all three act on targets that are NOT time-dependently lost, so all three give the same modest, delay-insensitive ~46%

g.title: cluster_third
g.text: 🛌 14. Third line — RSE anaesthesia. These act at sites that do not need γ2, so they still work; the cost moves from 'will it work' to 'what does it cost to keep it working'

g.title: cluster_steroid
g.text: 🧪 15. Neurosteroids and adjuncts — the pharmacology that follows from cluster 4, and the trial that shows why a correct target is not sufficient

g.title: cluster_resist
g.text: 🚧 16. Pharmacoresistance — TWO independent hypotheses. Only one of them is fixed by giving more drug

g.title: cluster_delay
g.text: ⏳ 17. THE DELAY CHAIN — the single most consequential variable in the model, and the only one that is entirely operational

g.title: cluster_endp
g.text: 🎯 18. Clinical endpoints — and the three dissociations that make SE trials so hard to read

g.title: cluster_chronic
g.text: 🕰️ 19. The tail — SE is also an epileptogenic event. The integrator that keeps running after the ICU discharge

g.title: LG3
g.text: R_SYN falls, NR_SYN rises, and the third
term is constant. Three curves, one clock.

g.title: LG4
g.text: Not to choose a drug — ESETT already showed
the choice is nearly free. It is to price a
MINUTE, and to say which drugs a minute costs
you (benzodiazepines) and which it does not
(second line), and which one it buys you
